8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

class AutoPruneStrategy {
    addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>) : void
    addNodeToTree(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>, currentNodeRef : node) : void
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(queue : Deque) : void
}
class BaseNode {
    content : String
    levelSeq : List<int>
    levelText : String
    title : String
    concatNode(node : BaseNode) : void
}
class ChainNode {
    patternPriority : int
}
class ChainParser {
    patterns : List<LevelPattern>
    createChainNode(levelSeq : List<int>, title : String, content : String, levelText : String, patternPriority : int) : ChainNode
    detectLevel(line : String) : ChainNode
    parseToChain(text : String) : List<ChainNode>
}
class LevelPattern {
    description : String
    failOnConvert : boolean
    fixedLevelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>
    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    regexText : String
    separator : String
    helper : ParserHelper
    convertMatchedText(matchedText : String) : List<EIntegerObject>
    getRegex() : Pattern
}

    convertNumber(numberType : NumberType, text : String) : EIntegerObject
    getNumberPattern(numberType : NumberType) : String
}

    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    prefixRegex : String
    separator : String
    suffixRegex : String
    build() : LevelPattern
    copySelf() : PatternBuilder
    modify(newPrefixRegex : String, newMinLevel : int) : PatternBuilder
    validate() : void
}
class StrictStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isChild(parentSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, childSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
}
class TreeBuilder {
    strategy : TreeBuildingStrategy
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
}
abstract class TreeBuildingStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    getLastLevel(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : int
    getPrefix(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : List<EIntegerObject>
    isImmNext(frontSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, backSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
    isRoot(node : BaseNode) : boolean
}
class TreeExporter {
    escapeJson(s : String) : String
    exportChain(chain : List<ChainNode>) : String
    exportToJson(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportToJsonFile(tree : TreeNode, filePath : Path) : void
    exportTree(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportTreeInternal(node : TreeNode, prefix : String, isLast : boolean, isRoot : boolean) : String
    nodeToDict(node : TreeNode) : EMap
    toJson(obj : EJavaObject, indent : int) : String
}
class TreeNode {
    children : List<TreeNode>
    parent : TreeNode
    addChild(child : TreeNode) : void
    getFullContent() : String
    mergeAllChildren() : void
}
enum NumberType {
    ARABIC
    ROMAN
    CHINESE
    LETTER
    CIRCLED
}

ChainNode --|> BaseNode
ChainParser *-- "*" LevelPattern : patterns
LevelPattern --> ParserHelper : helper
StrictStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy

TreeNode --|> BaseNode
TreeNode *-- "*" TreeNode : children  'opposite: parent
TreeNode --> TreeNode : parent  'opposite: children

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement**, a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML, and a list of operation specifications. Your task is to correct the specifications that are inconsistent with the requirement.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Read the requirement and the class diagram.
2. For each operation specification, determine whether it is complete and consistent with the requirement.
3. If there is any error, correct the erroneous specification.
4. Follow the specification format. Output changed specifications only; OMIT unchanged specifications.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.

# Operation Specifications
AutoPruneStrategy::buildTree
Summary: Constructs a document outline tree from a parsed chain using the auto-prune strategy. It creates a synthetic ROOT, maintains the latest valid branch, attaches immediate nodes, queues non-immediate nodes, and merges pending nodes according to the auto-prune rules.
Algorithm:
  1. Create root = createTreeNode(null). Set root.title = "ROOT"; currentBranch = [root]; pending = empty deque.
  2. For each ChainNode in chain:
     - If the ChainNode has an empty levelSeq, merge its content into root and continue.
     - If the node is an immediate valid next node relative to some ancestor in currentBranch:
         - First merge all pending nodes into currentBranch.last.content in arrival order.
         - Call addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node, currentBranch).
     - Otherwise:
         - Add node to the pending deque.
         - If pending.size() == 3:
             - If all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence, attach all of them using addNodeAndUpdateBranch in order.
             - Otherwise, merge the oldest pending node into currentBranch.last.content.
  3. After all chain nodes are processed, merge every remaining pending node into currentBranch.last.content.
  4. Return root.
Related Features: createTreeNode, addNodeAndUpdateBranch, addNodeToTree, isAllNotImmNodesSiblings, isRoot, isImmNext, getPrefix, getLastLevel
Related Classes: TreeNode, ChainNode, List, Deque
Input: chain — ordered list of ChainNodes from ChainParser.
Output: TreeNode — the synthetic root of the constructed tree.
Pre-condition: chain is non-null and ordered as parsed.
Post-condition: root title is "ROOT"; valid headings are attached; invalid or pending headings are merged into content in arrival order.

AutoPruneStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary: Creates a TreeNode from a ChainNode. If the ChainNode is null or has an empty levelSeq, a synthetic ROOT TreeNode is returned.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new TreeNode.
  2. If chainnode is null or chainnode.levelSeq is empty:
     - Set title to "ROOT", levelSeq to empty, levelText to "", content to "".
  3. Otherwise, copy title, content, levelSeq, and levelText from chainnode.
  4. Initialize children as empty and parent as null.
Related Features: None
Related Classes: TreeNode, ChainNode, List
Input: chainnode — ChainNode to convert, or null for root.
Output: TreeNode
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: The returned TreeNode has the same heading data as the ChainNode, or represents ROOT when chainnode is null/root-level.

AutoPruneStrategy::isAllNotImmNodesSiblings
Summary: Checks whether all pending ChainNodes in the deque form an immediate sibling sequence: they must share the same level-sequence prefix and their last level values must increase by exactly one in arrival order.
Algorithm:
  1. If the deque has fewer than three nodes, return.
  2. Let first = queue.peekFirst().
  3. For each subsequent node n:
     - getPrefix(n.levelSeq).equals(getPrefix(first.levelSeq))
     - getLastLevel(n.levelSeq) == getLastLevel(previousNode.levelSeq) + 1
  4. If all checks pass, the pending nodes are an immediate sibling sequence.
  5. Otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into content by the caller.
Related Features: getPrefix, getLastLevel, queue
Related Classes: ChainNode, Deque, List
Input: queue — Deque of pending ChainNodes.
Output: void; the check result is used by the caller to decide whether to attach or merge.
Pre-condition: queue is non-null and contains pending non-immediate ChainNodes.
Post-condition: The pending queue is not modified by this operation.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeToTree
Summary: Attaches a ChainNode to the tree without updating the current branch. This is the lower-level attachment step used when a node is known to be attachable.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a TreeNode from the ChainNode with createTreeNode(node).
  2. Start the search from currentNodeRef if it is non-null; otherwise start from the last element of currentBranch.
  3. Scan backwards through currentBranch to find the closest ancestor whose levelSeq is a prefix of node.levelSeq.
  4. Attach the new TreeNode to that ancestor using ancestor.addChild(treeNode).
  5. Leave currentBranch unchanged.
Related Features: createTreeNode, currentBranch, addChild on TreeNode
Related Classes: TreeNode, ChainNode, List
Input: node — ChainNode; currentBranch — current root-to-leaf path; currentNodeRef — the TreeNode from which upward search should begin, or null.
Output: void
Pre-condition: node is non-null and not a root node; currentBranch is non-empty.
Post-condition: a new TreeNode is inserted into the tree under the nearest prefix ancestor; currentBranch is not modified.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeAndUpdateBranch
Summary: Attaches a ChainNode as a new TreeNode under the closest ancestor in the current branch whose level sequence is a prefix of the new node's level sequence, then updates the current branch so that the new node becomes the new current node.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a TreeNode from the ChainNode with createTreeNode(node).
  2. Scan currentBranch from the last node toward the root.
  3. Find the first TreeNode whose levelSeq is a prefix of node.levelSeq; this is the parent.
  4. Call parent.addChild(treeNode).
  5. Remove all nodes after parent from currentBranch, then append treeNode to currentBranch.
Related Features: createTreeNode, addNodeToTree, currentBranch
Related Classes: TreeNode, ChainNode, List
Input: node — the ChainNode to attach; currentBranch — the list of TreeNodes representing the current root-to-leaf path.
Output: void
Pre-condition: node is not a root node; currentBranch is non-empty and contains the current root.
Post-condition: node's TreeNode is attached to the nearest prefix ancestor, and currentBranch ends with the newly added TreeNode.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

# Operation Specifications
ChainParser::detectLevel
Summary: Attempts to recognize a single input line as a heading. Patterns are tried in order; the first pattern that both matches the line and produces a valid level sequence determines the returned ChainNode. If no pattern works, returns null.
Algorithm:
  1. For each LevelPattern p in patterns, with zero-based index i:
     - Match the line using p.getRegex().
     - If no match, continue.
     - Convert the matched numbering text using p's conversion logic.
     - If conversion fails and p.failOnConvert is true, continue to the next pattern.
     - If conversion fails but a fixedLevelSeq is available, use fixedLevelSeq.
     - Reject the pattern if the resulting sequence is empty, contains non-positive values, or is outside p.minLevel/p.maxLevel.
     - Extract the title from the non-numbered part of the line.
     - Return createChainNode(seq, title, "", matchedNumberText, i).
  2. Return null if no pattern yields a valid heading.
Related Features: patterns, createChainNode
Related Classes: ChainParser, LevelPattern, ChainNode
Input: line — a single line of plain text.
Output: ChainNode — the recognized heading node, or null if the line is not a valid heading.
Pre-condition: line is non-null; patterns is ordered by priority.
Post-condition: The first valid pattern determines the returned node and its priority; unmatched lines return null.

ChainParser::createChainNode
Summary: Factory method that creates a ChainNode and initializes its heading fields.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new ChainNode.
  2. Set title, content, levelText, and patternPriority from the arguments.
  3. Copy levelSeq into a new list to prevent external mutation.
  4. Return the ChainNode.
Related Features: None
Related Classes: ChainNode, List
Input: levelSeq — list of integer heading levels; title — heading title; content — initial content text; levelText — raw numbering text; patternPriority — priority index of the matched pattern.
Output: ChainNode
Pre-condition: levelSeq and title are non-null.
Post-condition: The returned ChainNode contains the supplied values, and levelSeq is defensively copied.

ChainParser::parseToChain
Summary: Parses the whole plain-text document into an ordered list of ChainNodes. Non-heading lines are appended to the content of the current section. If content appears before any heading, a synthetic ROOT ChainNode is used.
Algorithm:
  1. Initialize result list and current = null.
  2. Split text into lines, preserving original line endings.
  3. For each line:
     - node = detectLevel(line).
     - If node != null:
         - If current != null, add current to result.
         - current = node.
     - Else:
         - If current == null, create a synthetic ROOT ChainNode with empty levelSeq, title "ROOT", content "", priority -1.
         - Append line to current.content.
  4. If current != null, add current to result.
  5. Return result.
Related Features: detectLevel, createChainNode
Related Classes: ChainParser, ChainNode, List
Input: text — the full input document as a String.
Output: List<ChainNode>
Pre-condition: text is non-null.
Post-condition: heading nodes are kept in encounter order; non-heading text is stored in the content of the applicable heading/root node.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.

# Operation Specifications
StrictStrategy::buildTree
Summary: Builds a document outline tree using strict parent-child validation. It rejects chains whose first heading is not a direct child of the ROOT.
Algorithm:
  1. Create root = createTreeNode(null); set current = root.
  2. For each ChainNode in chain:
     - If the ChainNode has an empty levelSeq, merge its content into root and continue.
     - Create TreeNode via createTreeNode(chainNode).
     - If current is not root and isChild(current.levelSeq, chainNode.levelSeq) is false, move upward through parents until a suitable parent is found or until the root is reached.
     - If no ancestor is a valid parent, throw an exception.
     - Otherwise attach the new TreeNode to that ancestor and set current to the new TreeNode.
  3. Return root.
Related Features: createTreeNode, isChild, isRoot
Related Classes: StrictStrategy, TreeNode, ChainNode
Input: chain — ordered list of ChainNodes.
Output: TreeNode
Pre-condition: chain is non-null.
Post-condition: Returns a valid strict tree or throws if the chain cannot be strictly attached to ROOT.

StrictStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary: Creates a TreeNode from a ChainNode. A null or root-level ChainNode produces the synthetic ROOT node.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new TreeNode.
  2. If chainnode is null or chainnode.levelSeq is empty, set title "ROOT", empty levelSeq/levelText/content.
  3. Otherwise copy title, content, levelSeq, and levelText from chainnode.
  4. Initialize children and parent.
Related Features: None

StrictStrategy::isChild
Summary: Checks whether childSeq is a direct child sequence of parentSeq.
Algorithm:
  1. If parentSeq or childSeq is null, return false.
  2. If childSeq.size() != parentSeq.size() + 1, return false.
  3. Return true if the first parentSeq.size() elements of childSeq equal parentSeq.
Related Features: None
Related Classes: List
Input: parentSeq — parent level sequence; childSeq — candidate child level sequence.
Output: boolean
Pre-condition: Both inputs are non-null level sequences.
Post-condition: Returns true only when childSeq extends parentSeq by exactly one level.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

{org.eclipse.emf.ecore.impl.EOperationImpl@79a13920 (name: buildTree) (ordered: true, unique: true, lowerBound: 0, upperBound: 1)=Summary: Builds a TreeNode outline from the chain using strict parent-child rules.
Algorithm:
  1. If chain is empty, create and return a synthetic root TreeNode titled "ROOT".
  2. If the first chain node is a root node (empty levelSeq), create the root with createTreeNode(); otherwise create a synthetic root.
  3. Initialize currentBranch with the root.
  4. For each remaining ChainNode:
     a. Convert it with createTreeNode().
     b. Search currentBranch from the end to the beginning for the deepest node whose levelSeq satisfies isChild(parentSeq, nodeSeq).
     c. If none exists, reject the chain with an exception.
     d. Attach the new node to that parent.
     e. Truncate currentBranch after the parent and append the new node.
  5. Return the root.
Related Features: createTreeNode(), isChild()
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, List
Input:
  - chain: List<ChainNode>; the parsed heading chain.
Output: TreeNode; the strict outline tree root, titled "ROOT".
Pre-condition: chain is not null.
Post-condition: Every attached node has a valid strict parent in the tree; invalid chains cause an exception instead of a malformed tree., org.eclipse.emf.ecore.impl.EOperationImpl@160b4809 (name: concatNode) (ordered: true, unique: true, lowerBound: 0, upperBound: 1)=Summary: Appends the content of another node to this node's content without inserting a separator.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
AutoPruneStrategy::buildTree
Summary: Builds a TreeNode outline from the chain using the tolerant auto-prune strategy.
Algorithm:
  1. Create an empty pending deque.
  2. If chain is empty, create and return a synthetic root TreeNode titled "ROOT" with empty levelSeq.
  3. If the first chain node is a root node (empty levelSeq), use createTreeNode() to make the root; otherwise create a synthetic root.
  4. Initialize currentBranch with the root only.
  5. For each remaining ChainNode in chain order, call addNodeToTree(node, currentBranch, currentBranch.last).
  6. After processing all nodes, merge any remaining pending nodes into currentBranch.last.content in arrival order.
  7. Return the root TreeNode.
Related Features: createTreeNode(), addNodeToTree(), pending, currentBranch
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, Deque, List
Input:
  - chain: List<ChainNode>; the parsed heading chain.
Output: TreeNode; the root of the constructed outline tree, always titled "ROOT".
Pre-condition: chain is not null.
Post-condition: The returned root contains all preserved headings and content; invalid non-recoverable pending headings have been merged into content.

AutoPruneStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary: Converts a ChainNode to a TreeNode by copying its structural data.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new TreeNode with the same title, levelSeq, levelText, and content as chainnode.
  2. Initialize children as an empty list and parent as null.
Related Features: None.
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, List
Input:
  - chainnode: ChainNode; the parsed heading node to convert.
Output: TreeNode; a tree node with the same title, levelSeq, levelText, and content.
Pre-condition: chainnode is not null.
Post-condition: The returned TreeNode is not yet connected to any parent or children.

AutoPruneStrategy::isAllNotImmNodesSiblings
Summary: Determines whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence.
Algorithm:
  1. If queue size is less than 2, return true.
  2. For each adjacent pair (a, b):
     a. The level sequences must have the same length.
     b. getPrefix(a.levelSeq) must equal getPrefix(b.levelSeq).
     c. getLastLevel(b.levelSeq) must equal getLastLevel(a.levelSeq) + 1.
  3. Return true if all adjacent pairs satisfy these conditions; otherwise return false.
Related Features: inherited getPrefix(), inherited getLastLevel(), queue elements' levelSeq
Related Classes: ChainNode, Deque, List, EIntegerObject
Input:
  - queue: Deque; the pending queue of ChainNodes to test.
Output: boolean; true if the pending nodes are consecutive siblings, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: queue is not null.
Post-condition: The queue is not modified.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeToTree
Summary: Processes one chain node using the auto-prune strategy. Immediate nodes are attached directly; non-immediate nodes are queued. When the pending queue reaches three nodes, the queue is either attached as a sibling sequence or the oldest pending node is merged into the current content.
Algorithm:
  1. If pending is empty and node is an immediate next node relative to currentBranch.last, call addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node, currentBranch) and return.
  2. If pending is non-empty and node is an immediate next node:
     a. Merge every pending node's content into currentNodeRef.content in arrival order.
     b. Clear pending.
     c. Call addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node, currentBranch) and return.
  3. Otherwise append node to pending.
  4. If pending.size() == 3:
     a. If isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(pending), attach all pending nodes in order using addNodeAndUpdateBranch, then clear pending.
     b. Otherwise remove the oldest pending node and merge its content into currentNodeRef.content.
Related Features: addNodeAndUpdateBranch(), isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(), pending, currentNodeRef.content
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, Deque, List
Input:
  - node: ChainNode; the heading node being processed.
  - currentBranch: List<TreeNode>; the current root-to-current path.
  - currentNodeRef: TreeNode; the current tree node whose content is the sink for merged discarded pending nodes.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: node is not null; currentBranch is non-empty; currentNodeRef is the last element of currentBranch.
Post-condition: The node is either attached, pending, or has been merged into the current content according to the auto-prune rule.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeAndUpdateBranch
Summary: Attaches a ChainNode to the current branch at the nearest suitable ancestor and updates the branch so that the new node becomes the current node.
Algorithm:
  1. Convert the ChainNode into a TreeNode using createTreeNode().
  2. Scan currentBranch from the end to the beginning.
  3. Choose the deepest candidate whose levelSeq is a proper prefix of node.levelSeq.
  4. Attach the new TreeNode to that candidate with addChild().
  5. Truncate currentBranch after that candidate and append the new TreeNode.
Related Features: createTreeNode(), currentBranch, node.levelSeq, TreeNode.addChild()
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, List
Input:
  - node: ChainNode; the heading node to attach. Must not be the synthetic root.
  - currentBranch: List<TreeNode>; the current root-to-current path, with the last element as the current node.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: node is not null; currentBranch is non-empty and contains at least the root.
Post-condition: node is connected to the nearest suitable ancestor in the tree, and currentBranch ends with the new TreeNode.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

# Operation Specifications
ChainParser::detectLevel
Summary: Detects whether a single line is a valid heading by trying patterns in order. Returns the first valid heading ChainNode, or null if the line is ordinary content.
Algorithm:
  1. For each pattern p in patterns, with 0-based index i:
     a. Use p.getRegex() to test the entire line.
     b. If the line matches, extract the matched numbering text and the title text.
     c. Convert the numbering text using p.convertMatchedText().
     d. If conversion fails or the resulting levelSeq is empty, skip this pattern.
     e. If levelSeq.size() is outside [p.minLevel, p.maxLevel], skip this pattern.
     f. Otherwise return createChainNode(levelSeq, title, "", matchedText, i).
  2. If no pattern yields a valid heading, return null.
Related Features: patterns, createChainNode(), LevelPattern.getRegex()
Related Classes: ChainNode, LevelPattern, Pattern, List
Input:
  - line: String; a single line of the document.
Output: ChainNode if the line is a recognized heading; otherwise null.
Pre-condition: line is not null; patterns is non-empty.
Post-condition: A non-null result is the first valid pattern's heading; a null result means the line must be treated as ordinary content.

ChainParser::createChainNode
Summary: Factory method that creates a ChainNode with all fields set.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new ChainNode.
  2. Copy levelSeq into the node.
  3. Set title, content, levelText, and patternPriority.
Related Features: None.
Related Classes: ChainNode, List
Input:
  - levelSeq: List<int>; the converted heading level sequence.
  - title: String; the heading title after the numbering prefix is removed.
  - content: String; the ordinary text content belonging to this node.
  - levelText: String; the original matched numbering text.
  - patternPriority: int; the 0-based priority of the matching pattern.
Output: ChainNode; a new parsed heading node.
Pre-condition: levelSeq, title, content, and levelText are not null; patternPriority is -1 for the synthetic root and >= 0 for real headings.
Post-condition: The returned ChainNode contains the supplied values; levelSeq is defensively copied.

ChainParser::parseToChain
Summary: Parses the whole plain-text document into a chain of heading nodes, preserving ordinary text as section content.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a synthetic root ChainNode with title "ROOT", empty levelSeq, empty levelText, patternPriority -1, and add it to the chain. Make it the current section.
  2. Iterate over the lines of text. Keep line endings that exist in the original text, but do not add extra separators.
  3. For each line:
     a. Call detectLevel(line).
     b. If it returns null, append the line to the current section's content.
     c. If it returns a heading ChainNode:
        i.   Store the accumulated content in the current section's content.
        ii.  Append the new heading to the chain.
        iii. Set the new heading as the current section.
        iv.  Clear the accumulated content buffer.
  4. After processing all lines, store the final accumulated content in the current section.
  5. Return the chain.
Related Features: detectLevel(), createChainNode()
Related Classes: ChainNode, List
Input:
  - text: String; the full plain-text document.
Output: List<ChainNode>; a never-empty chain beginning with the synthetic root if needed, followed by heading nodes in document order.
Pre-condition: text is not null.
Post-condition: Every recognized heading is represented; all unmatched lines are stored in the content of the current section.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

# Operation Specifications
StrictStrategy::buildTree
Summary: Builds a TreeNode outline from the chain using strict parent-child rules.
Algorithm:
  1. If chain is empty, create and return a synthetic root TreeNode titled "ROOT".
  2. If the first chain node is a root node (empty levelSeq), create the root with createTreeNode(); otherwise create a synthetic root.
  3. Initialize currentBranch with the root.
  4. For each remaining ChainNode:
     a. Convert it with createTreeNode().
     b. Search currentBranch from the end to the beginning for the deepest node whose levelSeq satisfies isChild(parentSeq, nodeSeq).
     c. If none exists, reject the chain with an exception.
     d. Attach the new node to that parent.
     e. Truncate currentBranch after the parent and append the new node.
  5. Return the root.
Related Features: createTreeNode(), isChild()
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, List
Input:
  - chain: List<ChainNode>; the parsed heading chain.
Output: TreeNode; the strict outline tree root, titled "ROOT".
Pre-condition: chain is not null.
Post-condition: Every attached node has a valid strict parent in the tree; invalid chains cause an exception instead of a malformed tree.

StrictStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary: Converts a ChainNode to a TreeNode by copying structural data.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new TreeNode with the same title, levelSeq, levelText, and content as chainnode.
  2. Set children to an empty list and parent to null.
Related Features: None.
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, List
Input:
  - chainnode: ChainNode; the node to convert.
Output: TreeNode; a disconnected copy of the chain node as a tree node.
Pre-condition: chainnode is not null.
Post-condition: The returned TreeNode has the same data fields and no parent or children.

StrictStrategy::isChild
Summary: Determines whether childSeq is an immediate child of parentSeq.
Algorithm:
  1. If childSeq.size() != parentSeq.size() + 1, return false.
  2. For each position i in parentSeq:
     a. If childSeq[i] != parentSeq[i], return false.
  3. Return true.
Related Features: None.
Related Classes: List, EIntegerObject
Input:
  - parentSeq: List<EIntegerObject>; the parent's level sequence.
  - childSeq: List<EIntegerObject>; the candidate child's level sequence.
Output: boolean; true if childSeq extends parentSeq by exactly one level.
Pre-condition: parentSeq and childSeq are not null.
Post-condition: No data is modified.

A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

# Operation Specifications
StrictStrategy::buildTree
Summary: Builds a TreeNode outline from the chain using strict parent-child rules.
Algorithm:
  1. If chain is empty, create and return a synthetic root TreeNode titled "ROOT".
  2. If the first chain node is a root node (empty levelSeq), create the root with createTreeNode(); otherwise create a synthetic root.
  3. Initialize currentBranch with the root.
  4. For each remaining ChainNode:
     a. Convert it with createTreeNode().
     b. Search currentBranch from the end to the beginning for the deepest node whose levelSeq satisfies isChild(parentSeq, nodeSeq).
     c. If none exists, reject the chain with an exception.
     d. Attach the new node to that parent.
     e. Truncate currentBranch after the parent and append the new node.
  5. Return the root.
Related Features: createTreeNode(), isChild()
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, List
Input:
  - chain: List<ChainNode>; the parsed heading chain.
Output: TreeNode; the strict outline tree root, titled "ROOT".
Pre-condition: chain is not null.
Post-condition: Every attached node has a valid strict parent in the tree; invalid chains cause an exception instead of a malformed tree.

StrictStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary: Converts a ChainNode to a TreeNode by copying structural data.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new TreeNode with the same title, levelSeq, levelText, and content as chainnode.
  2. Set children to an empty list and parent to null.
Related Features: None.
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, List
Input:
  - chainnode: ChainNode; the node to convert.
Output: TreeNode; a disconnected copy of the chain node as a tree node.
Pre-condition: chainnode is not null.
Post-condition: The returned TreeNode has the same data fields and no parent or children.

StrictStrategy::isChild
Summary: Determines whether childSeq is an immediate child of parentSeq.
Algorithm:
  1. If childSeq.size() != parentSeq.size() + 1, return false.
  2. For each position i in parentSeq:
     a. If childSeq[i] != parentSeq[i], return false.
  3. Return true.
Related Features: None.
Related Classes: List, EIntegerObject
Input:
  - parentSeq: List<EIntegerObject>; the parent's level sequence.
  - childSeq: List<EIntegerObject>; the candidate child's level sequence.
Output: boolean; true if childSeq extends parentSeq by exactly one level.
Pre-condition: parentSeq and childSeq are not null.
Post-condition: No data is modified.

# Operation Specifications
PatternBuilder::modify
Summary: Returns a modified copy of this builder with a new prefix regex and minimum level.
Algorithm:
  1. Call copySelf() to obtain a copy.
  2. Set the copy's prefixRegex to newPrefixRegex.
  3. Set the copy's minLevel to newMinLevel.
  4. Call validate() on the copy.
  5. Return the copy.
Related Features: copySelf(), validate(), prefixRegex, minLevel
Related Classes: PatternBuilder
Input:
  - newPrefixRegex: String; the replacement prefix regular expression.
  - newMinLevel: int; the replacement minimum level.
Output: PatternBuilder; a validated modified builder.
Pre-condition: newPrefixRegex is a valid regex fragment; 1 <= newMinLevel <= maxLevel.
Post-condition: The returned builder is independent and has the requested prefixRegex and minLevel.

PatternBuilder::validate
Summary: Validates the builder's configuration before constructing a LevelPattern.
Algorithm:
  1. Check that numberType is not null.
  2. Check that prefixRegex and suffixRegex are non-null and compile as valid regex fragments.
  3. Check that separator is non-null and non-empty.
  4. Check that minLevel >= 1 and maxLevel >= minLevel.
  5. Throw an appropriate exception if any check fails.
Related Features: numberType, prefixRegex, suffixRegex, separator, minLevel, maxLevel
Related Classes: NumberType, Pattern
Input: None.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: If the configuration is valid, the builder is unchanged; otherwise an exception is thrown.

PatternBuilder::copySelf
Summary: Creates an independent copy of this PatternBuilder.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new PatternBuilder.
  2. Copy maxLevel, minLevel, numberType, prefixRegex, separator, and suffixRegex into it.
  3. Return the copy.
Related Features: maxLevel, minLevel, numberType, prefixRegex, separator, suffixRegex
Related Classes: PatternBuilder, NumberType
Input: None.
Output: PatternBuilder; a new builder with identical field values.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: The original builder is unchanged; modifications to the returned copy do not affect the original.

# Operation Specifications
PatternBuilder::modify
Summary: Returns a modified copy of this builder with a new prefix regex and minimum level.
Algorithm:
  1. Call copySelf() to obtain a copy.
  2. Set the copy's prefixRegex to newPrefixRegex.
  3. Set the copy's minLevel to newMinLevel.
  4. Call validate() on the copy.
  5. Return the copy.
Related Features: copySelf(), validate(), prefixRegex, minLevel
Related Classes: PatternBuilder
Input:
  - newPrefixRegex: String; the replacement prefix regular expression.
  - newMinLevel: int; the replacement minimum level.
Output: PatternBuilder; a validated modified builder.
Pre-condition: newPrefixRegex is a valid regex fragment; 1 <= newMinLevel <= maxLevel.
Post-condition: The returned builder is independent and has the requested prefixRegex and minLevel.

PatternBuilder::validate
Summary: Validates the builder's configuration before constructing a LevelPattern.
Algorithm:
  1. Check that numberType is not null.
  2. Check that prefixRegex and suffixRegex are non-null and compile as valid regex fragments.
  3. Check that separator is non-null and non-empty.
  4. Check that minLevel >= 1 and maxLevel >= minLevel.
  5. Throw an appropriate exception if any check fails.
Related Features: numberType, prefixRegex, suffixRegex, separator, minLevel, maxLevel
Related Classes: NumberType, Pattern
Input: None.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: If the configuration is valid, the builder is unchanged; otherwise an exception is thrown.

PatternBuilder::copySelf
Summary: Creates an independent copy of this PatternBuilder.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new PatternBuilder.
  2. Copy maxLevel, minLevel, numberType, prefixRegex, separator, and suffixRegex into it.
  3. Return the copy.
Related Features: maxLevel, minLevel, numberType, prefixRegex, separator, suffixRegex
Related Classes: PatternBuilder, NumberType
Input: None.
Output: PatternBuilder; a new builder with identical field values.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: The original builder is unchanged; modifications to the returned copy do not affect the original.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
