# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

```plantuml

class AutoPruneStrategy {
    addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>) : void
    addNodeToTree(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>, currentNodeRef : node) : void
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(queue : Deque) : void
}
class BaseNode {
    content : String
    levelSeq : List<int>
    levelText : String
    title : String
    concatNode(node : BaseNode) : void
}
class ChainNode {
    patternPriority : int
}
class ChainParser {
    patterns : List<LevelPattern>
    createChainNode(levelSeq : List<int>, title : String, content : String, levelText : String, patternPriority : int) : ChainNode
    detectLevel(line : String) : ChainNode
    parseToChain(text : String) : List<ChainNode>
}
class LevelPattern {
    description : String
    failOnConvert : boolean
    fixedLevelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>
    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    regexText : String
    separator : String
    helper : ParserHelper
    convertMatchedText(matchedText : String) : List<EIntegerObject>
    getRegex() : Pattern
}
class ParserHelper {
    convertNumber(numberType : NumberType, text : String) : EIntegerObject
    getNumberPattern(numberType : NumberType) : String
}
class PatternBuilder {
    maxLevel : int
    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType
    prefixRegex : String
    separator : String
    suffixRegex : String
    build() : LevelPattern
    copySelf() : PatternBuilder
    modify(newPrefixRegex : String, newMinLevel : int) : PatternBuilder
    validate() : void
}
class StrictStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isChild(parentSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, childSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
}
class TreeBuilder {
    strategy : TreeBuildingStrategy
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
}
abstract class TreeBuildingStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    getLastLevel(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : int
    getPrefix(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : List<EIntegerObject>
    isImmNext(frontSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, backSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
    isRoot(node : BaseNode) : boolean
}
class TreeExporter {
    escapeJson(s : String) : String
    exportChain(chain : List<ChainNode>) : String
    exportToJson(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportToJsonFile(tree : TreeNode, filePath : Path) : void
    exportTree(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportTreeInternal(node : TreeNode, prefix : String, isLast : boolean, isRoot : boolean) : String
    nodeToDict(node : TreeNode) : EMap
    toJson(obj : EJavaObject, indent : int) : String
}
class TreeNode {
    children : List<TreeNode>
    parent : TreeNode
    addChild(child : TreeNode) : void
    getFullContent() : String
    mergeAllChildren() : void
}
enum NumberType {
    ARABIC
    ROMAN
    CHINESE
    LETTER
    CIRCLED
}

AutoPruneStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
ChainNode --|> BaseNode
ChainParser *-- "*" LevelPattern : patterns
LevelPattern --> ParserHelper : helper
StrictStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
TreeBuilder --> TreeBuildingStrategy : strategy
TreeNode --|> BaseNode
TreeNode *-- "*" TreeNode : children  'opposite: parent
TreeNode --> TreeNode : parent  'opposite: children
@enduml
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeBuilder::buildTree
Summary: Builds a tree by delegating to the configured TreeBuildingStrategy.
Algorithm:
  1. Invoke strategy.buildTree(chain).
  2. Return the resulting root TreeNode.
Related Features: strategy
Related Classes: TreeBuildingStrategy, TreeNode, ChainNode, List
Input:
  - chain: List<ChainNode>; the parsed heading chain.
Output: TreeNode; the root of the constructed outline tree.
Pre-condition: chain is not null and strategy is not null.
Post-condition: The returned tree is the result of the selected strategy.

# Operation Specifications
TreeNode::mergeAllChildren
Summary: Recursively collapses all descendant content into this node's content, then removes the children.
Algorithm:
  1. For each child, call child.mergeAllChildren().
  2. For each child in original order, call concatNode(child) to append the child's content.
  3. Clear this.children and set each removed child's parent to null.
Related Features: children, content, concatNode(), parent
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input: None.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: This node contains all descendant content in traversal order, and its child list is empty.

TreeNode::getFullContent
Summary: Returns the concatenated content of this node and all descendants in traversal order, without added separators.
Algorithm:
  1. Start with this.content.
  2. For each child in children order, append child.getFullContent().
  3. Return the concatenated string.
Related Features: content, children, getFullContent()
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input: None.
Output: String; the full content of the subtree rooted at this node.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: No data is modified.

TreeNode::addChild
Summary: Adds a child to this node and sets the child's parent pointer.
Algorithm:
  1. If child is null or already in children, do nothing.
  2. If child.parent is a different node, remove child from that old parent.
  3. Append child to this.children.
  4. Set child.parent to this.
Related Features: children, parent
Related Classes: TreeNode, List
Input:
  - child: TreeNode; the node to add as a child.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: child is not null.
Post-condition: child is the last child of this node, and child.parent points to this node.

```text
Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeNode::mergeAllChildren
Summary: Recursively collapses all descendant content into this node's content, then removes the children.
Algorithm:
  1. For each child, call child.mergeAllChildren().
  2. For each child in original order, call concatNode(child) to append the child's content.
  3. Clear this.children and set each removed child's parent to null.
Related Features: children, content, concatNode(), parent
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input: None.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: This node contains all descendant content in traversal order, and its child list is empty.

TreeNode::getFullContent
Summary: Returns the concatenated content of this node and all descendants in traversal order, without added separators.
Algorithm:
  1. Start with this.content.
  2. For each child in children order, append child.getFullContent().
  3. Return the concatenated string.
Related Features: content, children, getFullContent()
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input: None.
Output: String; the full content of the subtree rooted at this node.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: No data is modified.

TreeNode::addChild
Summary: Adds a child to this node and sets the child's parent pointer.
Algorithm:
  1. If child is null or already in children, do nothing.
  2. If child.parent is a different node, remove child from that old parent.
  3. Append child to this.children.
  4. Set child.parent to this.
Related Features: children, parent
Related Classes: TreeNode, List
Input:
  - child: TreeNode; the node to add as a child.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: child is not null.
Post-condition: child is the last child of this node, and child.parent points to this node.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeExporter::exportTreeInternal
Summary: Recursively renders a tree node and its descendants as an ASCII tree.
Algorithm:
  1. If isRoot is true, append node.title plus a newline.
  2. If non-root, append prefix, then "└── " if isLast else "├── ", then node.title plus a newline.
  3. Compute childPrefix as prefix plus "    " if isLast else "│   ".
  4. For each child in order, recurse with childPrefix and isLast = (i == children.size() - 1).
Related Features: node.title, node.children, exportTreeInternal()
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input:
  - node: TreeNode; the current node.
  - prefix: String; current indentation prefix.
  - isLast: boolean; whether this node is the last child of its parent.
  - isRoot: boolean; whether this node is the root.
Output: String; the ASCII tree fragment rooted at node.
Pre-condition: node and prefix are not null.
Post-condition: The output is deterministic and preserves order.

TreeExporter::exportToJsonFile
Summary: Writes the tree's JSON representation to a file.
Algorithm:
  1. Serialize tree into the stable JSON string using the four-space-indent JSON export format.
  2. Write the JSON string to filePath using UTF-8, overwriting any existing file.
Related Features: exportToJson(), nodeToDict(), toJson(), escapeJson()
Related Classes: TreeNode, Path, EMap, EJavaObject
Input:
  - tree: TreeNode; the root of the tree to export.
  - filePath: Path; the destination file path.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: tree and filePath are not null; the target location is writable.
Post-condition: The file contains the deterministic JSON tree output with four-space indentation.

TreeExporter::nodeToDict
Summary: Converts a TreeNode into a map suitable for JSON serialization.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a map.
  2. Put "title" -> node.title.
  3. Put "level_seq" -> a copy of node.levelSeq.
  4. Put "level_text" -> node.levelText.
  5. Put "content" -> node.content.
  6. Put "children" -> a list of nodeToDict(child) for each child in order.
  7. Return the map.
Related Features: node.title, node.levelSeq, node.levelText, node.content, node.children
Related Classes: TreeNode, EMap, EJavaObject, List
Input:
  - node: TreeNode; the tree node to convert.
Output: EMap; a map with keys title, level_seq, level_text, content, and children.
Pre-condition: node is not null.
Post-condition: The returned map is a snapshot; later tree mutations do not affect it.

TreeExporter::exportTree
Summary: Returns a human-readable ASCII rendering of the outline tree.
Algorithm:
  1. Call exportTreeInternal(tree, "", true, true).
  2. Return the resulting string.
Related Features: exportTreeInternal()
Related Classes: TreeNode
Input:
  - tree: TreeNode; the root of the tree to export.
Output: String; a stable ASCII tree representation.
Pre-condition: tree is not null.
Post-condition: The output contains one line per node and preserves child order.

    if (childSeq.size() != parentSeq.size() + 1)
    {
      return false;
    }

    // 2. For each position i in parentSeq, the corresponding childSeq value must match.
    for (int i = 0; i < parentSeq.size(); i++)
    {
      if (!childSeq.get(i).equals(parentSeq.get(i)))
      {
        return false;
      }
    }

    // 3. Return true.
    return true;
  }

```java
   * Summary: Builds a TreeNode outline from the chain using the tolerant auto-prune strategy.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Create an empty pending deque.
   *   2. If chain is empty, create a synthetic root TreeNode titled "ROOT", with empty levelSeq, empty content, and no children, and return it.
   *   3. Let startIndex = 0.
   *      If the first chain node has an empty levelSeq, create the root with createTreeNode(chain.get(0)) and set startIndex = 1.
   *      Otherwise create a synthetic root TreeNode titled "ROOT", with empty levelSeq, empty content, and no children.
   *   4. Initialize currentBranch as a list containing only root.
   *   5. For i = startIndex to chain.size() - 1, call addNodeToTree(chain.get(i), currentBranch, currentBranch.last).
   *   6. After processing all nodes, merge any remaining pending nodes into currentBranch.last.content in arrival order, concatenating content without extra separators.
   *   7. Return root.
   * Related Features: createTreeNode(), addNodeToTree(), pending, currentBranch

   * Input:

   * Output: TreeNode; the root of the constructed outline tree. If a synthetic root was created, its title is "ROOT"; if the first chain node was a root node, that node's title is used.
   * Pre-condition: chain is not null.

   * Summary: Processes one chain node using the auto-prune strategy. Immediate nodes are attached directly; non-immediate nodes are queued. When the pending queue reaches three nodes, the queue is either attached as a sibling sequence or the oldest pending node is merged into the current content.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If pending is empty and isImmNext(currentBranch.last.levelSeq, node.levelSeq) is true, call addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node, currentBranch) and return.
   *   2. If pending is not empty and isImmNext(currentBranch.last.levelSeq, node.levelSeq) is true:
   *      a. Merge every pending node's content into currentNodeRef.content in arrival order, without extra separators.

   *   4. If pending.size() == 3:
   *      a. If isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(pending), attach all pending nodes in order using addNodeAndUpdateBranch, then clear pending.
   *      b. Otherwise remove the oldest pending node and merge its content into currentNodeRef.content.
```

        EList<Integer> nodeSeq = node.getLevelSeq();

   *      b. getPrefix(a.levelSeq) must equal getPrefix(b.levelSeq).
   *      c. getLastLevel(b.levelSeq) must equal getLastLevel(a.levelSeq) + 1.
   *   3. Return true if all adjacent pairs satisfy these conditions; otherwise return false.
   * Related Features: inherited getPrefix(), inherited getLastLevel(), queue elements' levelSeq
   * Related Classes: ChainNode, Deque, List, EIntegerObject
   * Input:
   *   - queue: Deque; the pending queue of ChainNodes to test.
   * Output: boolean; true if the pending nodes are consecutive siblings, false otherwise.
   * Pre-condition: queue is not null.
   * Post-condition: The queue is not modified.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model queueDataType="edu.arborparser.Deque&lt;edu.arborparser.ChainNode&gt;"
   *        annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(final Deque<ChainNode> queue)
```java
  {
```
```java
    if (queue.size() < 2)
    {
      return true;
    }
    ChainNode previous = null;
    for (ChainNode node : queue)
    {
      if (previous != null)
      {
        EList<Integer> previousSeq = previous.getLevelSeq();
        EList<Integer> nodeSeq = node.getLevelSeq();
        if (previousSeq.size() != nodeSeq.size())
        {
          return false;

          return false;
        }
        if (getLastLevel(nodeSeq) != getLastLevel(previousSeq) + 1)
        {
          return false;
        }
      }
      previous = node;
    }
    return true;
```

   *   2. If pending is not empty and isImmNext(currentBranch.last.levelSeq, node.levelSeq) is true:
   *      a. Merge every pending node's content into currentNodeRef.content in arrival order, without extra separators.
   *      b. Clear pending.
   *      c. Call addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node, currentBranch) and return.
   *   3. Otherwise append node to pending.
   *   4. If pending.size() == 3:
   *      a. If isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(pending), attach all pending nodes in order using addNodeAndUpdateBranch, then clear pending.
   *      b. Otherwise remove the oldest pending node and merge its content into currentNodeRef.content.
   * Related Features: isImmNext(), addNodeAndUpdateBranch(), isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(), pending, currentBranch, currentNodeRef.content
   * Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, Deque, List
   * Input:
   *   - node: ChainNode; the heading node being processed.
   *   - currentBranch: List<TreeNode>; the current root-to-current path.
   *   - currentNodeRef: TreeNode; the current tree node whose content is the sink for merged discarded pending nodes.
   * Output: None.
   * Pre-condition: node is not null; currentBranch is non-empty; currentNodeRef is the last element of currentBranch.
   * Post-condition: The node is either attached, pending, or has been merged into the current content according to the auto-prune rule.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model currentBranchMany="true" currentNodeRefDataType="edu.arborparser.node"
   *        annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void addNodeToTree(final ChainNode node, final EList<TreeNode> currentBranch, final TreeNode[] currentNodeRef)
  {
    TreeNode current = currentBranch.get(currentBranch.size() - 1);
    if (pending.isEmpty() && isImmNext(current.getLevelSeq(), node.getLevelSeq()))
    {
      addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node, currentBranch);
      return;
    }
    if (!pending.isEmpty() && isImmNext(current.getLevelSeq(), node.getLevelSeq()))
    {
      for (ChainNode pendingNode : pending)
      {
        currentNodeRef[0].setContent(currentNodeRef[0].getContent() + pendingNode.getContent());
      }
      pending.clear();
      addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node, currentBranch);
      return;
    }
    pending.addLast(node);
    if (pending.size() == 3)
    {
      if (isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(pending))
      {
        for (ChainNode pendingNode : pending)
        {
          addNodeAndUpdateBranch(pendingNode, currentBranch);
        }
        pending.clear();
      }
      else
      {
        ChainNode oldest = pending.removeFirst();
        currentNodeRef[0].setContent(currentNodeRef[0].getContent() + oldest.getContent());
      }
    }
  }

  public void addNodeAndUpdateBranch(final ChainNode node, final EList<TreeNode> currentBranch)
  { ... /* omitted */ }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Determines whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If queue size is less than 2, return true.
   *   2. For each adjacent pair (a, b):
   *      a. The level sequences must have the same length.
   *      b. getPrefix(a.levelSeq) must equal getPrefix(b.levelSeq).
   *      c. getLastLevel(b.levelSeq) must equal getLastLevel(a.levelSeq) + 1.
   *   3. Return true if all adjacent pairs satisfy these conditions; otherwise return false.
   * Related Features: inherited getPrefix(), inherited getLastLevel(), queue elements' levelSeq
   * Related Classes: ChainNode, Deque, List, EIntegerObject
   * Input:
   *   - queue: Deque; the pending queue of ChainNodes to test.
   * Output: boolean; true if the pending nodes are consecutive siblings, false otherwise.
   * Pre-condition: queue is not null.
   * Post-condition: The queue is not modified.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model queueDataType="edu.arborparser.Deque&lt;edu.arborparser.ChainNode&gt;"
   *        annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(final Deque<ChainNode> queue)
  {
    if (queue.size() < 2)
    {
      return true;
    }
    ChainNode previous = null;
    for (ChainNode node : queue)
    {
      if (previous != null)
      {
        EList<Integer> previousSeq = previous.getLevelSeq();
        EList<Integer> nodeSeq = node.getLevelSeq();
        if (previousSeq.size() != nodeSeq.size())
        {
          return false;
        }
        if (!getPrefix(previousSeq).equals(getPrefix(nodeSeq)))
        {
          return false;
        }
        if (getLastLevel(nodeSeq) != getLastLevel(previousSeq) + 1)
        {
          return false;
        }
      }
      previous = node;
    }
    return true;
  }

  private Deque<ChainNode> pending = new ArrayDeque<ChainNode>();

} // AutoPruneStrategy
